title: What Is Vibe Coding? Build Software with AI

scenes.narration: Imagine building an app by describing what you want in plain English, instead of writing every line of code yourself. An AI assistant generates the code, you run it, explain what is wrong, and ask for changes. That approach is commonly called vibe coding. It can make software creation more accessible, but there is an important catch: code that looks right is not necessarily code that works.

visual.title: What is vibe coding?
visual.subtitle: Describe it. Generate it. Test it.

scenes.narration: Here is the basic workflow. First, describe the problem and what the finished app should do. Second, ask the AI to generate a solution. Third, run the code and observe what actually happens. Fourth, give the AI specific feedback and improve the result. You repeat that cycle until the software behaves as expected. Think of the AI as a coding assistant, not a magic button.

visual.title: The basic workflow
items: Run it and observe the result

scenes.narration: Suppose you want a simple task list. You could prompt an AI: build a web page where I can add tasks, mark them complete, and remove them. Keep the design simple, explain the files you create, and tell me how to run the app. The AI may generate HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. You open the page, try adding a task, and check whether every button does what you requested.

visual.title: A better coding prompt
visual.code:
Build a task list web app.
Allow users to add tasks,
mark them complete, and delete them.
Explain each file and how to run it.

cues: Suppose you want a simple task list

scenes.narration: Vibe coding can help beginners turn ideas into prototypes, help experienced developers explore options quickly, and reduce the amount of repetitive code people write by hand. It is especially useful for experimenting and learning. But speed during the first draft does not guarantee quality when the project becomes larger, more complex, or important to other people.

Here is where you need to be careful. AI can produce bugs, misunderstand requirements, use unsafe patterns, or introduce unnecessary dependencies. A feature may work in one example and fail in another. You might also end up with code you cannot explain or maintain. And you should never paste passwords, private API keys, or confidential information into an AI tool without understanding its data policies.

visual.title: What can go wrong?
items: Code that is hard to maintain

scenes.narration: So how do you use it responsibly? Break a large idea into small tasks. Ask the AI to explain important changes. Read the code differences before accepting them. Run tests, try unusual inputs, and keep your work under version control with Git so you can review changes and recover earlier versions. Before deploying, check security and configuration carefully. For a real application, you remain responsible for the code you ship.
cues: Break a large idea into small tasks

scenes.narration: The key lesson is simple. Vibe coding lets you describe an idea and collaborate with AI to create software faster. That is powerful, but generating code is only one part of engineering. Reliable software also requires understanding, testing, security, and maintenance. Learn to use AI to accelerate your thinking, not replace it. Next, we will explore how the internet works and how information travels between devices.

visual.title: Remember these three things
items: AI can help turn ideas into code
